about: Design rules a model checks a UI-builder design against. Each rule quotes the guidance it comes from and links its source: a page on developer.android.com or m3.material.io, the Android Knowledge Base for agent skills, a component set in the Wear OS Material 3 Figma kit, or the androidx source whose KDoc it quotes. `check` is a yes/no question where YES means the design follows the rule. `kind` is `structure` when the design tree is enough evidence, `visual` when it needs a picture of the design. Candidates are extracted with scripts/guidelines/extract-guidance.mjs and reviewed by a person before they are added here. Visual rules say which picture to judge: the device picture (the first frame on the watch) or the unrolled picture (the whole scrolling content, scrolled to the end so a revealed edge button shows). `surfaces` (optional) narrows a rule to `screen` or `widget` designs on its platform; a rule without it applies to every surface.

rules.guidance: Accommodate Time Text if used, but don't overlap the top section of the page.
rules.check: Judge this on the device picture (the first frame, as the wearer first sees it). Is the time text at the top of the screen clear of any overlapping content?

rules.guidance: To reinforce that the device is a watch, we recommend showing the time text even when in an app journey (optional, but recommended).
rules.check: Does a design built on a wear-m3/screen-scaffold set its timeText? Answer not_applicable for widgets, dialogs, confirmations and pickers.

rules.guidance: Margins should be defined in percentages to avoid clipping and provide proportional scaling of elements.
rules.check: Is every piece of text, every icon and every control drawn whole, with none of its pixels missing? Answer fail only when part of a glyph, an icon or a control's own shape is visibly cut off in a picture: a letter sliced, an icon missing a side, a button's edge flattened where the edge or a container covers it. Being close to the edge, or to a curve, is not clipping, and neither is a container's own rounded outline. For a screen, judge round-edge clipping on the device picture, and clipping inside components on the unrolled picture when one is attached; content that continues below the bottom of the device picture in a scrolling list is not clipped. For a widget, look at the Samsung and the Pixel Watch pictures, and answer fail only for content cut in one of them; name which picture in your reason.

rules.guidance: Don't use components with a fixed width that don't fill the screen responsively or adjust the behavior of content to fill the available space. We recommend using percentage margins so the size of the margins adapts to the growing curve of the display.
rules.check: Do buttons and cards in the screen's content slot fill the available width, with no fixed width or size modifier? Answer not_applicable for widgets and for icon buttons, which are meant to size to their content.

rules.guidance: Use a Column as a direct child of ScreenScaffold only if the screen will never scroll, even with the largest system font.
rules.check: If the screen-scaffold's content is a plain layout/column rather than a transforming-lazy-column, is it short enough (a few short items) that it would still fit at the largest font size? Answer not_applicable when the content is a scrolling list.

rules.guidance: Dialogs should be direct in communicating information and dedicated to completing a task.
rules.check: If this design is a dialog or confirmation, does it communicate one thing and offer only the actions needed to complete that one task? Answer not_applicable when it is not a dialog.

rules.guidance: Reserves at least 48.dp in size to disambiguate touch interactions if the element would measure smaller. This uses the Material recommended minimum size of 48.dp x 48.dp.
rules.check: Is the tap area of every tappable control at least 48dp in each direction? Count the padding Wear adds to compact and extra-small buttons and icon buttons (their tap area is 48dp even when they draw smaller); flag only controls given a fixed size or height that leaves the tap area under 48dp.

rules.guidance: Color roles come in pairs (container and on-container) that provide a minimum of 3:1 color contrast. Custom colors should keep that contrast.
rules.check: Where the design overrides colors, does it pair each container color with its matching content (on-) role, or with colors that are clearly high contrast?

rules.guidance: All empty states should have a clear call-to-action so the user knows what to do to fix a potential issue, or find out more information.
rules.check: If this design shows an empty, error or signed-out state, does it offer a clear action? Answer not_applicable when it does not show such a state.

rules.guidance: Never hide a gesture-only action. A visible element that performs the same task must be present.
rules.check: Does every action bound to a gesture (long press, swipe, double tap) also have a visible control that performs it?

rules.guidance: Always supply your widget's background brush directly to WearWidgetDocument so the host system can paint and mask the background to the native OEM container shape. Setting a transparent or black canvas and drawing a custom rounded container inside the layout can cause floating box and letterboxing defects on some devices.
rules.check: If this design is a widget (its root is a widget-container), is its background set on the widget container's background property rather than drawn by a coloured or rounded box inside the content? Answer not_applicable when it is not a widget.

rules.guidance: Ensure your root container composable uses RemoteModifier.fillMaxSize(). Because container DP dimensions and safe insets vary across watch models, hardcoding fixed dimensions or outer padding can cause clipping or misaligned layouts.
rules.check: If this design is a widget, does the content directly inside the widget container fill it (fillMaxSize), with no fixed width, height or outer padding? Answer not_applicable when it is not a widget.

rules.guidance: Tiles should feel focused, concise, and purpose-driven. Avoid providing a superfluous amount of functionality, and refrain from using more than one interactive component to trigger a specific action. (Tiles guidance; widgets replace Tiles.)
rules.check: If this design is a widget, does it focus on one task, with no two controls doing the same thing? Answer not_applicable when it is not a widget.

rules.guidance: We don't recommend using containers for decorative or structural purposes, to avoid taps that don't do anything.
rules.check: If this design is a widget, does every container that looks like a button (filled, rounded and button-shaped) have an action or click binding? Treat an empty or placeholder click handler as an action. Answer not_applicable for app screens, where non-interactive cards are fine.

rules.guidance: If a card has an action, it should only contain a single action. Don't have multiple buttons within a card.
rules.check: Does every card contain at most one button or action?

rules.guidance: Don't have more than one list per view; this is overwhelming visually and focus wise.
rules.check: Does the screen contain at most one list?

rules.guidance: Don't use title chips as a tapable action prompt, since they do not have a focus state; use a button instead.
rules.check: Are title chips used only as labels, never with a click or tap action?

rules.guidance: Don't grow the button group past 10 buttons. Don't stack multiple button groups. Don't group buttons of different heights together.
rules.check: Does each button group have 10 or fewer buttons of one height, with no button group stacked on another?

rules.guidance: Don't use a button as a static decorative element. Don't use a toggle button for non binary actions. Don't overwhelm the user's view with too many buttons.
rules.check: Does every button have an action, and is every toggle a true on/off choice?

rules.guidance: Surfaces must be black for highest contrast. Don't use bright or filled surfaces. Don't fill the screen with all white, as this can cause thermal mitigation.
rules.check: Are the surfaces black or transparent, with no large bright or white areas?

rules.guidance: Don't use color text for all content. Don't use overly saturated colors.
rules.check: Is colored text kept for emphasis only, with body text in the default foreground color and no overly saturated colors?

rules.guidance: Use unfilled icons to avoid halation, or light bleed. Use a heavier stroke weight and rounded icon variants; avoid thin strokes.
rules.check: Are icons outlined (unfilled) and rounded, with no thin-stroke icons?

rules.guidance: Anchor elements to the bottom of the canvas, to build upwards. Content should avoid being centered vertically.
rules.check: Is the content anchored to the bottom of the frame rather than floating at the top or center?

rules.guidance: This button represents the most important action on the screen, and must take the whole width of the screen as well as being anchored to the screen bottom.
rules.check: Is there at most one wear-m3/edge-button, placed in the screen-scaffold's edgeButton slot rather than inside a list or layout? Answer not_applicable when there is no edge-button.

rules.guidance: EdgeButton has 4 standard sizes, taking 1 line of text for the extra small, 2 for small and medium, and 3 for the large. Optionally, a single icon can be used instead of the text.
rules.check: Does the edge-button's content fit its size: one short line of text (or a single icon) for size=extra-small, at most two lines for small and medium, at most three for large? Answer not_applicable when there is no edge-button.

rules.guidance: This is a high-emphasis button for the primary, most important or most common action on a screen.
rules.check: When the screen has two or more wear-m3/button actions, is variant=filled kept for the one primary action, with the others filled-tonal, outlined or child? Answer not_applicable with fewer than two buttons.

rules.guidance: ChildButton is a low-emphasis button for optional or supplementary actions with the least amount of prominence.
rules.check: Is a button with variant=child never the only action or the primary action on the screen? Answer not_applicable when no child buttons are used.

rules.guidance: Title styles are not recommended for interactive components, rather page headings or sub headings. Label styles are applied to interactive components.
rules.check: Does text inside buttons and cards use label or body styles, with title styles kept for headings outside controls? Answer not_applicable when no text style is set inside a control.

rules.guidance: Numeral text styles are used for numerical digits, usually limited to a few characters, where no localization is required.
rules.check: Is every text with a numeral style purely digits, a time or a short number (no words)? Answer not_applicable when no numeral styles are used.

rules.guidance: Do NOT hard-code text sizes, use typography from MaterialTheme. Do NOT hard-code colors, use colorScheme.
rules.check: Do text nodes set a style rather than fontSizeSp, lineHeightSp or letterSpacingSp, and do colours come from the theme's colour roles rather than hex values on individual components? Theme-level overrides on the screen-scaffold (theme*Color, theme*Typeface) are fine.

rules.guidance: Only use the scroll-indicator on scrolling screens. Remember to add the scroll-indicator on scrolling screens.
rules.check: Is the screen-scaffold's scrollIndicator on exactly when its content is a scrolling list (transforming-lazy-column)? Answer not_applicable for widgets and designs without a screen-scaffold.

rules.guidance: Don't display the time on a temporary dialog, confirmation overlay or a picker.
rules.check: When the design is an alert dialog, confirmation or picker (date-picker, time-picker), is timeText left unset? Answer not_applicable for other designs.

rules.guidance: Use both icons and labels when possible. Don't rely solely on icons to prompt the user to take action.
rules.check: Are icon-only controls (icon-button, icon-only edge-button) kept to universally recognisable actions (add, close, play, settings), with other actions labelled? Answer not_applicable when there are no icon-only controls.

rules.guidance: Container roles are used as a fill color for foreground elements like buttons. They shouldn't be used for text or icons.
rules.check: Is no *Container colour role (primaryContainer, secondaryContainer, tertiaryContainer, errorContainer) used as a text colour, icon tint or contentColor? Answer not_applicable when the design names no colour roles.

rules.guidance: When subtitle is used content shouldn't exceed 2 lines height. Overall the title, content and subtitle text should be no more than 5 rows of text combined.
rules.check: Does each wear-m3/card with variant=title hold at most 5 rows of text in total? Answer not_applicable when there are no title cards.

rules.guidance: It should be used when the user will be presented with a binary decision. Where user input is not required, such as displaying a transient success or failure message, use ConfirmationDialog. The title should not exceed 3 lines.
rules.check: If this design is an alert dialog (wear-m3/alert-dialog), does it pose a yes/no decision with a title of 3 lines or fewer, rather than a status message that needs no input? Answer not_applicable for other designs.

rules.guidance: Recommendation is while using this flag do not have more than MaxSegmentSteps steps.
rules.check: Does a segmented wear-m3/slider (segmented=segmented) have 8 steps or fewer? Answer not_applicable when there is no segmented slider.

rules.guidance: ListHeaders are typically expected to be a few words of text on a single line.
rules.check: Is each wear-m3/list-header a few words on one line? Answer not_applicable when there are no list headers.

rules.guidance: Because partial-height widgets integrate directly into a vertically scrolling surface, this fixed bottomSlot paradigm no longer exists, and migrating requires a deliberate UI redesign rather than a direct component swap.
rules.check: If this design is a widget, does it avoid remote-m3/remote-edge-button, using an inline button or a whole-container tap instead? Answer not_applicable when it is not a widget.

rules.guidance: Rather than porting a dense, full-screen Tile layout one-to-one, streamline your design to emphasize primary information within the main content area.
rules.check: If this design is a widget, does it lead with one primary piece of information rather than a dense grid of equal items? Answer not_applicable when it is not a widget.

rules.guidance: The actions in this Tile are unclear: where does the container with the album art take the user, and is that different from the Play button?
rules.check: If this design is a widget, is no clickable card or container wrapping a button that does something different? Answer not_applicable when it is not a widget.

rules.guidance: If you do not hide the app title on small screen, and have two rows, the height of the components will not adhere to our accessibility standards.
rules.check: If this design is a small widget (remote-m3/widget-container-small, 76dp tall), does it avoid stacking a title above a row of tap targets, or two rows of tap targets? Answer not_applicable for other designs.

rules.guidance: Show only one primary piece of information at a time (for example, using a Stack). Avoid multiple simultaneous cards.
rules.check: Is at most one card shown outside a Stack or List?

rules.guidance: If the items are of different types use a stack. If the items are of the same type, use a list. Don't use a title chip with a stack.
rules.check: Do Lists hold items of one type and Stacks mixed types, with no TitleChip on a Stack? Answer not_applicable when there is neither.

rules.guidance: Scrolling containers like lists should be the only major component on a screen. Avoid placing a scrollable list directly above or below other interactive elements, such as buttons.
rules.check: Is a List free of sibling buttons directly above or below it? Answer not_applicable when there is no list.

rules.guidance: Never embed a card within a List Item.
rules.check: Does no ListItem contain a Card? Answer not_applicable when there are no list items.

rules.guidance: Leave onClick as null if the Card contains multiple internal interactive elements, to avoid focus contention.
rules.check: Does every clickable Card contain no buttons of its own? Answer not_applicable when no card is clickable.

rules.guidance: Always center text in a title chip. Never let the title chip go to two lines. Keep the label to three words or less.
rules.check: Is every TitleChip label three words or fewer, on one line? Answer not_applicable when there are no title chips.

rules.guidance: If an icon serves as a trigger, then you must use an IconButton.
rules.check: Does every tappable icon use an IconButton rather than a clickable Icon? Answer not_applicable when no icon is tappable.

rules.guidance: NEVER use pure black (#000000) for icon tints.
rules.check: Is no icon tinted #000000?

rules.guidance: Don't use a determinate indicator when the processing time is unknown. Keep to one progress indicator at a time.
rules.check: Is there at most one progress indicator, indeterminate when it shows loading of unknown length? Answer not_applicable when there are none.

rules.guidance: While background, surface, outline, and outlineVariant are marked as customizable, we strongly recommend that you don't customize these values.
rules.check: Are the background, surface, outline and outlineVariant colour roles left at their defaults? Answer not_applicable when the design overrides no colour roles.

rules.guidance: Always use a consistent background color and corner radius for every item. Don't vary these unless you are visually grouping different types of content.
rules.check: Do the items of each List share one background and shape? Answer not_applicable when there is no list.

rules.guidance: Instead of just stretching or shrinking UI elements in response to different window sizes, adaptive apps replace layout components and show or hide content.
rules.check: Comparing the phone and tablet pictures, does the tablet picture change the layout to use the extra width (a different navigation component, an extra pane, more columns, or content revealed) rather than showing the phone layout simply stretched wider? Answer not_applicable when the design is only a dialog or sheet.

rules.guidance: The default behavior is to show a navigation bar if the width or height is compact or if the device is in tabletop posture, and a navigation rail for everything else.
rules.check: In the phone picture, if the screen offers top-level app destinations, are they shown in a bottom navigation bar (m3/navigation-bar) rather than a navigation rail or a permanently open drawer that takes width from the compact screen? Answer not_applicable when the screen has no top-level navigation.

rules.guidance: Change UI components as the window size changes to take advantage of available display space. For example, swap the bottom navigation bar used on compact window sizes for a vertical navigation rail on medium and expanded windows.
rules.check: In the tablet picture, if the screen offers top-level app destinations, are they shown in a navigation rail or navigation drawer on the leading edge, rather than in a bottom navigation bar stretched across the full width? Answer not_applicable when the screen has no top-level navigation.

rules.guidance: Compact sizes should stick to a one pane layout. Medium can use 1–2 pane layouts. Large and extra-large can use multiple pane layouts.
rules.check: In the phone picture, is the content shown as a single pane, with no two panes squeezed side by side into the compact width?

rules.guidance: Create multi-pane layouts (where appropriate) to take advantage of large screen space.
rules.check: In the tablet picture, if the screen holds a collection with details, or main content with related supporting content, is it shown in two or more panes side by side rather than one pane filling the window? Answer not_applicable for a single focused task such as a form, a sign-in screen or a full-screen media view.

rules.guidance: Expanded-width displays accommodate both the list and detail at the same time. Medium- and compact-width displays show either the list or the detail, depending on user interaction with the app.
rules.check: If the design is a list of items that open to details (messages, contacts, files, settings), does the tablet picture show the list and the detail side by side while the phone picture shows only one of them? Answer not_applicable when the design is not a list-detail screen.

rules.guidance: The list and detail are shown together, and the list indicates that the item corresponding to the content in the detail pane is selected. If just the list pane was visible and the window widens to expanded, the list and a placeholder detail pane are shown together.
rules.check: In the tablet picture of a list-detail screen, does the list visibly mark the item whose details fill the detail pane, or, when nothing is selected, does the detail pane show a placeholder rather than being left blank? Answer not_applicable when the tablet picture shows no list-detail panes.

rules.guidance: For medium width, split the display space equally between the main and supporting content. For expanded width, give 70% of the space to the main content, 30% to the supporting content.
rules.check: In the tablet picture, if the design shows main content beside a supporting pane, is the main content the wider pane (roughly 70% of the width) and the supporting pane the narrower one (roughly 30%)? Answer not_applicable when there is no supporting pane.

rules.guidance: A feed layout supports displays of almost any size because the grid can adapt from a single, scrolling column to a multi-column scrolling feed of content.
rules.check: If the design is a feed or gallery of equivalent cards or tiles, does the tablet picture show more columns than the phone picture, rather than the same single column made wider? Answer not_applicable when the design is not a feed or gallery.

rules.guidance: The key to an adaptive feed is the columns configuration. GridCells.Adaptive(minSize = 180.dp) creates a grid where each column is at least 180.dp wide. The grid then displays as many columns as can fit in the available space.
rules.check: If the design is a feed or gallery of equivalent items, is it built on a grid whose column count follows the available width (an adaptive or minimum-size column setting, or columns chosen per window size class) rather than a fixed column count or a plain layout/lazy-column? Answer not_applicable when the design is not a feed or gallery.

rules.guidance: Do set a max width on content and components to prevent stretching full width. Don't allow content to stretch full width.
rules.check: In the tablet picture, is the body content held to a sensible width (by a max width, panes or columns), rather than single-column cards, list rows or images stretched across the whole 1280dp window?

rules.guidance: If you're not using content panes, don't just stretch UI elements to fill available display space. Long lines of text are difficult to read.
rules.check: In the tablet picture, are paragraphs of body text set in a column narrow enough to read comfortably, rather than running in long lines across most of the window width? Answer not_applicable when the design has no multi-line body text.

rules.guidance: Buttons are not full width on large screens.
rules.check: In the tablet picture, is every button sized to its label or to a constrained column or pane, with none stretched across the full width of the window?

rules.guidance: Text fields and boxes don't stretch to full width on large screens.
rules.check: In the tablet picture, are text fields and search boxes held to a bounded width, with none stretched across the full width of the window? Answer not_applicable when the design has no text input.

rules.guidance: Stretched buttons look poorly designed. If you use Modifier.fillMaxWidth, don't assume that's the right behavior for all display sizes.
rules.check: Where buttons, text fields, cards or body text use fillMaxWidth, is that width bounded on wide windows, by a max width (widthIn) on them or on an enclosing column, or by a pane or grid cell they sit in? Answer not_applicable when nothing uses fillMaxWidth.

rules.guidance: Bottom sheets are not full width on large screens. (Apply a maximum width to avoid stretching.) Allow a component to change its presentation. For example, a bottom sheet can become a side sheet at larger sizes.
rules.check: In the tablet picture, if the design shows a bottom sheet, is it held to a maximum width (or presented as a side sheet) rather than spanning the full window width? Answer not_applicable when there is no sheet.

rules.guidance: Small edit menus or modals don't cover the entire screen and maintain context for the user as much as possible.
rules.check: In the tablet picture, does every dialog, menu or small modal appear as a bounded surface with the screen behind it still visible, rather than covering the entire window? Answer not_applicable when the design has no dialog, menu or modal.

rules.guidance: Ensure all touch targets are at least 48 dp, even if this extends past the UI element visual.
rules.check: Is every interactive element at least 48dp in both dimensions, or given a 48dp minimum interactive size, with no size, height or width modifier shrinking a clickable element's touch area below 48dp?

rules.guidance: Avoid adding tap gestures or drag targets under system insets; these conflict with edge-to-edge and gesture navigation. Don't place critical UI at the very edge of the screen.
rules.check: In both pictures, are text, icons and controls clear of the status bar, the navigation bar and any display cutout area, with nothing interactive placed under them or hard against the screen edge?

rules.guidance: A standard margin value for compact sizing is 16 dp, but margins should adapt to accommodate larger screens. Your app's body content and actions must stay within and align with these margins.
rules.check: Comparing the phone and tablet pictures, does body content sit inside consistent side margins (about 16dp on the phone, wider on the tablet), with content and actions aligned to those margins rather than touching the window edge?

rules.guidance: To allow users to adjust the font size, specify font size in scalable pixels (sp). Don't make the body size any smaller than 12 sp. This guideline aligns with the Material typescale as a default.
rules.check: Is every text size taken from the theme's type scale or given in sp, with no body text set smaller than 12sp?

rules.guidance: Images are displayed at a proper resolution and are not stretched or cropped.
rules.check: In the tablet picture, are images shown at their natural aspect ratio, not stretched, distorted or cropped to a thin strip by a container that grew wider than on the phone? Answer not_applicable when the design has no images.

rules.guidance: Build from black. Watches are designed with a black background, instead of the tinted background that phones use.
rules.check: Is the screen's background left black (the theme's default background), rather than filled with a tinted, coloured or bright surface behind the content? Containers such as buttons and cards may use their own colours. Answer not_applicable for widgets, whose background the widget container paints.

rules.guidance: Buttons with (2) on primary on (1) primary and (4) on primary container on (3) primary container stay legible as the contrast level changes. Buttons with (2) primary dim on (1) primary or (4) primary dim on (3) primary container become illegible as contrast levels shift.
rules.check: Where a button or card sets its container and content colours, is content on a primary container coloured onPrimary, and content on a primaryContainer coloured onPrimaryContainer, never primaryDim or primaryContainer? Answer not_applicable when the design names no colour roles.

rules.guidance: Prioritize content. Place the most important information at the top of the screen.
rules.check: Judge this on the device picture (the first frame, as the wearer first sees it). Is the screen's most important information (its title, the key value or the main control) at the top of that frame, rather than below secondary content or off the first frame?

rules.guidance: Focus on one or two tasks at a time rather than a full app experience. Don't create complex and detailed apps such as a calendar grid.
rules.check: Does the screen serve one or two tasks with a few actions, rather than packing a dense grid, table or many unrelated controls onto the watch? A scrolling list of similar choices (a menu or settings list) is fine.

rules.guidance: Button: Primary label (1-3 lines); Secondary label (1-2 lines). (Text properties of the Button component set in the Wear OS Material 3 Design Kit.)
rules.check: Does each wear-m3/button keep its label to 3 lines or fewer and its secondaryLabel to 2 lines or fewer at the device width? Answer not_applicable when there are no buttons.

rules.guidance: Card: Title text (1-2 lines). (A text property of the Card component set in the Wear OS Material 3 Design Kit.)
rules.check: Does each wear-m3/card keep its title to 2 lines or fewer at the device width? The body's budget is wear.card.text-budget's. Answer not_applicable when there are no cards.

rules.guidance: The filled button style has the most visual impact after the FAB, and should be used for important, final actions that complete a flow, like Save, Join now, or Confirm. Since they have such strong emphasis, the filled style should be used sparingly, ideally for only one action on a page.
rules.check: Is at most one action on the screen a filled button (m3/button with style=filled, or Button), with the other buttons tonal, outlined or text? Answer not_applicable when there are fewer than two buttons.

rules.guidance: Label text is the most important element of a button. It should be very brief, ideally 1–3 words. Don’t truncate or wrap label text. It should always be fully visible on a single line.
rules.check: Is every button label (m3/button and its tonal, outlined, elevated and text forms) a few words that fit on one line, with no wrapping or ellipsis? Answer not_applicable when there are no labelled buttons.

rules.guidance: Don't display multiple FABs on a single screen. Individual components, such as cards, shouldn't have their own FAB.
rules.check: Is there at most one FAB (m3/button with style=fab, or a floating or extended floating action button) on the screen, placed on the screen or in the navigation rail rather than inside a card, list item or other container? Answer not_applicable when there is no FAB.

rules.guidance: Use FABs for primary, positive actions. Don’t use FABs for minor, overflow, unclear, or destructive actions. Use clear and simple icons such as add, message, or edit.
rules.check: Does the FAB perform the screen's primary, constructive action (create, compose, add, edit), with a clear icon, rather than a minor, overflow or destructive action such as delete or settings? Answer not_applicable when there is no FAB.

rules.guidance: The extended FAB’s label should clearly describe its action. Use 1–2 words at most. An extended FAB can't have an icon without a text label.
rules.check: Does every extended floating action button carry a text label of one or two words? Answer not_applicable when there is no extended FAB.

rules.guidance: Avoid putting more than five navigation items in a navigation bar. Don’t remove the labels from navigation items. Don’t use a navigation bar for fewer than three destinations. Instead, use tabs. All navigation items require a label text. It should be 1-2 words.
rules.check: If the screen has a navigation bar, or a navigation-suite-scaffold that shows its items as a bar on the phone, does it hold three to five items, each with an icon and a label of one or two words? Answer not_applicable when there is no top-level navigation.

rules.guidance: The collapsed nav rail runs along the leading edge of the window, and should contain 3–7 navigation items. Labels should be short enough to not be truncated.
rules.check: If the screen has a navigation rail, or a navigation-suite-scaffold that shows its items as a rail on the tablet, does it hold three to seven items with short labels? Answer not_applicable when there is no top-level navigation.

rules.guidance: One navigation destination is always active. Don’t use the active indicator for more than one destination at a time.
rules.check: Among the items of each navigation bar, rail or navigation-suite-scaffold, is exactly one selected? Answer not_applicable when there is no top-level navigation.

rules.guidance: A navigation rail should be the only visible navigation element. Never use the navigation rail and navigation bar simultaneously.
rules.check: Does the screen show one top-level navigation element, never a navigation bar together with a navigation rail? Answer not_applicable when there is no top-level navigation.

rules.guidance: The toolbar and navigation bar are both placed at the bottom of the window, so should not be shown at the same time. Show the navigation bar on primary pages, and toolbars on subsequent pages with actions.
rules.check: Is no bottom or docked toolbar shown on the same screen as a navigation bar? Answer not_applicable when the screen has no toolbar or no navigation bar.

rules.guidance: App bars should only have one action, two if necessary. Up to two icon buttons can be placed after the headline, aligned to the trailing edge of the app bar. Don’t put multiple filled or tonal buttons in the app bar.
rules.check: Does each top app bar carry at most two trailing actions, with at most one of them filled or tonal? Answer not_applicable when there is no top app bar, or for a search app bar, which may also show an avatar.

rules.guidance: Visually emphasizing a single action more than others is an effective way to create hierarchy and guide people to controls they use most often. Avoid emphasizing more than one action at a time. Don’t use square filled icon buttons in floating toolbars.
rules.check: In each toolbar (horizontal or vertical floating toolbar), is at most one control emphasised (filled, or a FAB beside it), with the rest standard icon buttons? Answer not_applicable when there is no toolbar.

rules.guidance: Dialogs should contain a maximum of two actions. If a single action is provided, it must be an acknowledgement action. If two actions are provided, one must be a confirming action, and the other a dismissing action. The confirmation button is always closest to the edge.
rules.check: If the design shows a dialog (m3/dialog or an alert dialog), does it offer at most two actions, a confirming one at the trailing end and a dismissing one before it (or a single acknowledgement)? Answer not_applicable when there is no dialog, or for a full-screen dialog.

rules.guidance: A dialog’s purpose should be communicated by its headline and buttons or actionable items. Avoid apologies (“Sorry for the interruption”), alarm (“Warning!”), or ambiguity (“Are you sure?”). This dialog title poses a specific question, concisely explains what’s involved in the request, and provides clear actions.
rules.check: If the design shows a dialog, does its title say specifically what is being decided, and does its confirming button name the action (Delete, Send, Create) rather than OK, Done or Yes? A single acknowledgement button may say OK. Answer not_applicable when there is no dialog.

rules.guidance: Only one snackbar may be displayed at a time. Avoid adding icons to snackbars. Snackbars can display a single text button that lets users take action on a process performed by the app. Don’t use a filled or elevated button in a snackbar, as it draws too much attention. On mobile, the text label can be up to two lines long.
rules.check: If the design shows a snackbar, is it the only one, with a message of two lines or fewer, no icon, and at most one text-style action? Answer not_applicable when there is no snackbar.

rules.guidance: Don’t display a single chip by itself. Chips should appear in a set. Avoid replacing major actions with chips. Actions that progress people to the next or previous step should always be displayed as buttons. Chip label text should be 20 characters or fewer.
rules.check: Do chips (filter, assist, input and suggestion chips) appear in sets of two or more, with labels of 20 characters or fewer, and is no step-completing action (Next, Submit, Save) a chip instead of a button? Answer not_applicable when there are no chips.

rules.guidance: Avoid using more than four tabs at once. At five or more tabs, the container becomes cramped. Don’t use tabs with both icons and text labels on only some tabs, but not others. Secondary tabs should always be placed below primary tabs.
rules.check: Does each fixed tab row (primary or secondary tab row) hold four tabs or fewer, do all its tabs use the same kind of label (all text, all icons, or all both), and is any secondary tab row below a primary one? Scrollable tab rows may hold more. Answer not_applicable when there are no tabs.

rules.guidance: Don’t scroll within a card to reveal information. Cards shouldn’t contain content that can be swiped, such as an image carousel or pagination. On a mobile device, cards can't internally scroll, as it could cause two scroll bars to be displayed.
rules.check: Is every card free of scrolling or swipeable content inside it (a lazy list, a scrolling column, a carousel or a pager)? Answer not_applicable when there are no cards.

rules.guidance: Container – Roles used as a fill color for foreground elements like buttons. They should not be used for text or icons. Don’t use the outline color for dividers since they have different contrast requirements. Instead, use outline variant.
rules.check: Is no *Container colour role (primaryContainer, secondaryContainer, tertiaryContainer, errorContainer) used as a text colour, icon tint or contentColor, and do dividers use outlineVariant rather than outline? Answer not_applicable when the design names no colour roles.

rules.guidance: To ensure accessible visual contrast in your app, apply colors only in the intended pairs or layering orders described in the following sections. Improper color mappings can produce unintended visual results and break accessibility.
rules.check: Where the design overrides a container or background colour, is its content given the matching on- role (onPrimary on primary, onSecondaryContainer on secondaryContainer, onSurface on a surface) or a colour of clearly high contrast? Answer not_applicable when the design overrides no colours.

rules.guidance: When multiple items are loading, use a single progress indicator to show progress for the group. Don’t add progress indicators to every activity. Avoid applying progress indicators to every button in a list.
rules.check: Does the screen show one progress or loading indicator for content that is loading together, rather than one on every item, card or button? Answer not_applicable when there are no progress or loading indicators.

rules.guidance: Every text field should have a label. Label text shouldn’t take up multiple lines. When using both variants of text fields, don't use both next to each other or within the same form.
rules.check: Does every text field have a short, one-line label, and does each form use one text field style (all filled or all outlined)? A search bar's placeholder counts as its label. Answer not_applicable when there are no text fields.

rules.guidance: By default, all buttons in a standard group should be the same size (XS to XL) and shape (round or square). Avoid mixing color styles in connected button groups. Button groups should move through layouts together in a single line. They shouldn’t wrap to a second line.
rules.check: Do the buttons in each button group or segmented button row share one size and shape, with a connected group using one colour style, and does the group sit on a single line? Answer not_applicable when there are no button groups.

rules.guidance: At compact breakpoints, only show up to three carousel items if they have text. Avoid exceeding two lines of text in carousel items at compact breakpoints unless the background is simple, like a single color.
rules.check: In the phone picture, does each carousel show at most three items when they carry text, with no more than two lines of text on any item? Answer not_applicable when there is no carousel.
